module_title: Advanced Analysis - Planetary Winds, Local Winds, and Cyclones
introduction: This advanced level explores the primary planetary wind systems that dictate global climate, the highly specific local winds driven by topography, and the rotational mechanics of Cyclones and Anticyclones.

core_concepts.title: Planetary (Permanent) Winds
core_concepts.description: 1. Trade Winds: Blow from the Sub-Tropical High (30°) towards the Equatorial Low (0°). Because of Coriolis, they blow from the North-East in the NH and South-East in the SH. 2. Westerlies: Blow from the Sub-Tropical High (30°) to the Sub-Polar Low (60°). They are incredibly strong in the Southern Hemisphere (called Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, Screaming Sixties). 3. Polar Easterlies: Cold winds blowing from the Poles (90°) to the Sub-Polar Low (60°).

core_concepts.title: Important Local Winds (Hot)
core_concepts.description: 1. Chinook ('Snow Eater'): A warm, dry wind descending the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains (USA/Canada), melting snow rapidly. 2. Foehn: Similar to Chinook, but in the Alps (Europe). 3. Sirocco ('Blood Rain'): A hot, dusty wind blowing from the Sahara Desert across the Mediterranean to Italy, often carrying red sand. 4. Loo: Extremely hot and dry summer wind in the northern plains of India.

core_concepts.title: Important Local Winds (Cold)
core_concepts.description: 1. Mistral: A violent, cold wind blowing from the Alps down into France and the Mediterranean Sea. 2. Blizzard: Severe, blinding snowstorms with very strong cold winds (common in polar and tundra regions).

core_concepts.title: Cyclones and Anticyclones
core_concepts.description: A Cyclone is a system of enclosed winds rotating around a 'Low Pressure' center. Due to the Coriolis effect, cyclones rotate Counter-Clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere. An Anticyclone rotates around a 'High Pressure' center, rotating Clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere (bringing clear weather).

important_entities.name: Jet Streams
important_entities.significance: Jet streams are fast-flowing, narrow, meandering air currents found in the upper troposphere (about 9-12 km high). They move from West to East and play a massive role in global weather, aviation routing, and particularly in influencing the arrival of the Indian Monsoon.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners love testing cyclone rotation. Memorize this firmly: In the Northern Hemisphere, cyclones rotate Anti-Clockwise. In the Southern Hemisphere, they rotate Clockwise. (It is exactly the opposite for Anticyclones).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Match the following is guaranteed here. Associate Chinook with the Americas (Rocky Mountains) and Foehn with Europe (Alps).

exam_strategy_tips: The terms 'Roaring Forties' and 'Furious Fifties' refer strictly to the 'Westerlies' in the Southern Hemisphere, where the lack of landmass allows the winds to reach extreme speeds.
The 'Blood Rain' associated with the Sirocco wind in Italy is a classic, highly-tested geographical trivia fact.
